newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond primary mart looks strong in '97.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond primary mart looks strong in '97.

text.p: Market players were looking forward to a strong market for new U.S. corporate bond issues next year, as the primary market remained quiet during the remaining days of 1996.

Junk players said they were enthusiastic about data released on Thursday that showed cash inflows into high-yield mutual funds remain strong. Mutual funds money is an important source of demand for new junk issues, they noted.
AMG Data Services reported inflows into junk mutual funds were a healthy $310 million for the past week, a market source said. An official at AMG Data would not comment.

While a large junk bond forward calendar is building for 1997, no new deals are expected to hit the market for the first several weeks after the holidays, as issuers and dealers will be conducting road shows.
This lack of supply, coupled with continuing strong demand, is likely to create extermely favorable market conditions when new junk deals are eventually priced, noted one market player.
New supply of investment-grade bonds is also expected to remain strong as a result of a continued benign interest rate environment, syndicate officials said.
